name: stri_remove_empty
title: Remove empty strings from a character vector

origin.description: Drops empty strings. Also drops missing values when na_empty is TRUE.

arguments.name: na_empty
arguments.text: Whether missing values should be treated as empty strings.

origin.details: Empty strings are removed. Missing values stay unless na_empty is identical to TRUE. stri_omit_empty is the same function. stri_remove_empty_na always drops both. A blank space is not an empty string.
origin.example:
stri_remove_empty(stri_na2empty(c('a', NA, '', 'b')))
stri_remove_empty(c('a', NA, '', 'b'))
stri_remove_empty(c('a', NA, '', 'b'), TRUE)

translation.description: Drops empty strings. Also drops missing values when na_empty is True.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: A string, or a list of strings and stringi._na.NA.

arguments.name: na_empty
arguments.text: Only the boolean True also drops missing values. Any other value, including 1, leaves them in place.

translation.details: An empty string is empty and is removed. NA is not empty, so it stays unless na_empty is True. The test is identity with True, matching R's identical(na_empty, TRUE). stri_omit_empty is this function.
translation.value: A list of the kept strings and missing values.
translation.example:
from stringi._na import NA
from stringi.utils import stri_na2empty, stri_remove_empty
print(stri_remove_empty(stri_na2empty(['a', NA, '', 'b'])))
print(stri_remove_empty(['a', NA, '', 'b']))
print(stri_remove_empty(['a', NA, '', 'b'], True))
